rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a critical design choice: multimodal vs single-modality. Config_016 tests multimodal (rna + image) with basic encoders (pca_n2000, resnet50) and simple fusion (concat), isolating the impact of combining modalities. This clarifies whether multimodal approaches provide value without overcomplicating the model, aligning with the principle of balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence from config_016 shows that multimodal singleprofile with pca_n2000 and resnet50 using concat fusion achieves 0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. This directly addresses a key design choice with potential to inform future configurations efficiently.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with singleprofile and pca_n2000 + resnet50 have similar validation accuracy (0.526 vs 0.523). This experiment tests whether a simpler rna_only model (config_001) can achieve comparable performance, isolating the impact of multimodal fusion. It directly addresses whether the added complexity of multimodal approaches provides meaningful gains, which is critical for resource allocation under budget constraints.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models (config_016) outperform rna_only models (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching to multiprofile in a multimodal setup (config_018) improves performance, isolating the impact of profile setting. It directly extends the current best configuration by changing a key design choice, balancing exploration and exploitation while focusing on a critical factor.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 encoders, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_019) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion method. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses a key design choice with minimal changes to the already high-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion yield high performance (config_019: 0.639 accuracy). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more complex model) further improves performance, isolating the effect of the image encoder choice. This is the best next step as it explores a key design choice with minimal variable changes, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.638999). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, isolating the effect of aggregation method. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly compares two critical design choices (avgpool vs. transformer) with minimal changes, providing insights into which aggregation method benefits the model more.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more complex representation) improves performance, isolating the effect of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing structure with exploration of a key design decision.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieves high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more complex model) while keeping other components the same would further improve performance. This isolates the effect of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision with sparse evidence in the current history.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion unchanged) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method on a proven high-performing configuration, balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of critical design choices.
